criteria.thresholds: ODD: >=4/8 symptoms for >=6 months (DSM p.522). IED: 2x/week x 3 months (A1) OR 3 outbursts in 12 months (A2), age >=6 (DSM p.527-528). Kleptomania/Pyromania: recurrent episodes (DSM p.537, p.539).
subtypes: ODD Severity: Mild (1 setting), Moderate (2 settings), Severe (3+ settings) (DSM p.523)

epidemiology.prevalence: ODD ~3.3% (DSM p.524); IED 1-yr 2.6%, lifetime 4.0% (DSM p.528); Kleptomania 0.3-0.6% (DSM p.540); Pyromania <0.1% (DSM p.538)
epidemiology.sex_ratio: ODD: 1.59:1 M:F pre-puberty, 1:1 in adolescence (DSM p.524); IED: M>=F (DSM p.528); Kleptomania: 1:3 M:F (3:1 females) (DSM p.540); Pyromania: M>>F (DSM p.538)
epidemiology.onset_age_typical: ODD: ~6 years / preschool (DSM p.525, Dulcan p.202); IED: late childhood/adolescence (DSM p.528); Kleptomania: adolescence (DSM p.540); Pyromania: late adolescence (DSM p.538)
epidemiology.heritability: ~74% variance in disruptive behavior traits (Dulcan p.200)
comorbidities: IED + PTSD (41% lifetime suicide attempt rate) (DSM p.529)
epidemiology.prognosis: ODD: Irritable mood predicts anxiety/MDD; Defiant behavior predicts CD (DSM p.525, Dulcan p.202). IED: persistent chronic course (DSM p.528).

etiology.genetic: Shared genetic vulnerability across ODD, CD, ADHD (~74% heritability); candidate genes DRD2, DBH, DAT1, NET1, androgen receptor (Dulcan p.200)
etiology.neurobiology: Frontolimbic dysfunction: Amygdala hyperresponsiveness, reduced ACC/OFC gray matter & top-down inhibition (DSM p.528, StahlNeuro p.539, p.577); Guanfacine acts on alpha-2A PFC receptors (StahlNeuro p.483-484); Naltrexone blocks ventral striatum dopamine (StahlNeuro p.571)
etiology.environmental: Patterson's coercion model (negative reinforcement of coercive loops) (Dulcan p.201); harsh/inconsistent parenting, trauma (DSM p.525, p.528)

first_line: ODD: Parent Management Training (PMT) + Child Problem-Solving Skills Training (PSST/CPS) (Dulcan p.203-204, p.901)
IED: CBT Anger Management (Dulcan p.597) + SSRIs (Fluoxetine 10-40 mg/d, Sertraline 25-150 mg/d) (DSM p.528, StahlKids p.208, p.467)
Kleptomania: CBT (Aversive covert sensitization, ERP) (StahlNeuro p.575-577)
second_line: ODD with ADHD: Guanfacine ER (0.05-0.12 mg/kg/d) (StahlKids p.245, Dulcan p.714) / Psychostimulants (Methylphenidate) (Dulcan p.203)
IED: Lithium Carbonate (0.6-1.2 mEq/L) (Dulcan p.763, StahlKids p.296) / Valproate (50-100 mcg/mL) (Dulcan p.768) / Topiramate (Dulcan p.126)
Kleptomania: Naltrexone (50-150 mg/d off-label) (StahlNeuro p.571, Dulcan p.126)
Severe Aggression: Risperidone (0.25-3.0 mg/d) / Aripiprazole (2-15 mg/d) (Dulcan p.816, StahlKids p.36, p.465)
key_side_effects: Guanfacine/Clonidine: Sedation, hypotension, bradycardia, rebound hypertension on abrupt stop (StahlKids p.244, Dulcan p.712)
Lithium: Tremor, polyuria, hypothyroidism, renal toxicity (StahlKids p.296)
Risperidone: Weight gain, hyperprolactinemia, metabolic syndrome (StahlKids p.465)
treatment.monitoring: Guanfacine: BP & HR at baseline and titration (StahlKids p.244). Lithium: blood level (0.6-1.2 mEq/L), BUN/Cr, TSH (Dulcan p.763, StahlKids p.296). Valproate: blood level (50-100 mcg/mL), LFTs, CBC (Dulcan p.768).

items: K-SADS-PL (Gold standard semi-structured interview for ages 6-18) (Dulcan p.68, p.88)
CBCL / ASEBA (Achenbach system, T-score >=67 indicates severe dysregulation) (Dulcan p.203, p.294)
Conners 3 / Vanderbilt scales (ADHD/ODD/CD rating scales) (Dulcan p.70, p.181)
ECBI / SESBI-R (Intensity and Problem scores for disruptive behavior) (Dulcan p.203)
OAS / MOAS / CAS (Overt aggression scales) (Dulcan p.213, p.304, p.593)
ARI (Affective Reactivity Index for irritability) (DSM p.845)
key_numbers: 4+ out of 8 symptoms required for ODD (DSM p.522)
6 months minimum duration for ODD (DSM p.522)
2x per week for 3 months (IED criterion A1) (DSM p.527)
3 outbursts in 12 months (IED criterion A2) (DSM p.527)
T-score >=67 on CBCL Dysregulated Phenotype (Dulcan p.294)

items: DMDD: Chronic daily irritability + severe outbursts >=3x/wk; DMDD hierarchy rules out ODD and IED (DSM p.178, p.526, p.528)
ADHD: Inattention/impulsivity non-compliance without hostile intent (DSM p.526)
Conduct Disorder: Proactive/predatory aggression, property destruction, theft; can be comorbid with ODD (DSM p.525, p.530)
TBI / Complex Partial Epilepsy: Organic brain injury causing personality change aggressive type (DSM p.530, Dulcan p.594)
PCP / Cocaine / Steroids: Substance-induced aggression ('Roid rage') (DSM p.25, p.530, p.596)
PANDAS / PANS: Acute onset aggression/rage following streptococcal/immune infection (Dulcan p.375, p.439)
key_numbers: 3+ outbursts per week in DMDD (DSM p.178)
Age >=6 minimum for IED diagnosis (DSM p.528)
6 months maximum for Adjustment Disorder after stressor (DSM p.525)

high_yield: DMDD diagnostic hierarchy completely excludes ODD and IED if chronic daily irritability is present (DSM p.178, p.526, p.528).
ODD threshold: >=4/8 symptoms for >=6 months; <5 years old requires symptoms on most days, >=5 years requires >=1x/week (DSM p.522).
IED criteria: A1 (mild/frequent) = verbal/physical non-damaging aggression 2x/week for 3 months; A2 (severe) = 3 property damage or injury outbursts in 12 months; minimum age 6 (DSM p.527-528).
IED + PTSD comorbidity carries a 41% lifetime suicide attempt rate (DSM p.529).
Kleptomania is 3x more common in females (3:1 F:M ratio), contrasting with most impulse-control disorders (DSM p.540).

Guanfacine ER dose in peds: 0.05-0.12 mg/kg/day; alpha-2A agonist in PFC improving signal-to-noise ratio; must monitor BP/HR and NEVER stop abruptly due to rebound hypertension (Dulcan p.712, p.714, StahlKids p.242-245).
Naltrexone (50-150 mg/day) blocks endogenous opioid-mediated dopamine release in ventral striatum, reducing kleptomania urges (Dulcan p.126, StahlNeuro p.571).

Impulsive aggression (IED) involves autonomic arousal and frontolimbic deficit (54-63%), whereas predatory aggression (CD) is instrumental and planned without arousal (17-29%) (StahlNeuro p.577, p.914).
